summary: BiChat generation moves to out-of-process execution whenever Redis is configured: send requests enqueue jobs onto the bichat:run:jobs stream and become event-log cursor readers, a RunJobWorker boots in every process that builds the module (consumer-group fan-out, XPENDING/XCLAIM crash handoff, one retry for infrastructure faults), and sends landing behind an active run park on a per-session FIFO with a queued sidebar status instead of failing with ErrActiveRunExists. The generation loop is extracted into a RunExecutor shared by the inline path (still used when Redis is unconfigured or an enqueue fails) and the worker. Also: money accounts return a field-level duplicate account number message instead of a raw SQL unique-violation error, and the client messages tab shows a localized empty state when no messages exist.
